terra.problem: Verse 17 itself says Jerusalem drained the goblet to the dregs; the explanation instead says the next verses show how much she drank.
It presents sorrow as what someone feels around the cup, though the text does not say that.
The statement that no one can guide Jerusalem is in verse 18, not the verse before it.
It says the sons are not moving and that a net holds an antelope still. The verse says they have fainted and lie like an antelope in a net, but does not say they are motionless.
It makes the sons' fainting the reason the LORD does not give them the cup. The text does not give that reason.
The text says the watchmen shout for joy, but does not say they are not holding cups.
“I think we can say once that this one is heavy” refers to the writing rule rather than speaking naturally to the baker.
It says the verse that follows shows how Jerusalem responded, but the description of her making her back like the ground is in the same verse.
It places Jerusalem staggering in the street. The passage says her sons lie at the head of every street, not that Jerusalem staggers there.
“There's no price tag” goes beyond the LORD's words. He says Jerusalem will be redeemed without money, not that there is no price of any kind.
It gives a desire as God's reason for speaking. The text says what His people will know, not that He says this because He wants them to know.
“That's their whole announcement” overlooks the verse's other descriptions of the messengers proclaiming peace and salvation.
The text says the LORD has comforted His people and redeemed Jerusalem. It does not say the ruins themselves have been comforted.
“Everyone gets to see it” expands the text's statement that all the ends of the earth will see God's salvation.
“No fleeing” removes the qualification. The text says they will not flee in haste.
The text does not say the watchmen are not guarding the back of the group.
